title: Counting the number of $1_{m}$-preperiodic $\mathcal{O}_{K}$-points of a discrete dynamical system with applications from arithmetic statistics, VII
summary: In this follow-up article of a multi-part series on (strictly) preperiodic point-counting, we inspect an astonishing relationship between the set of (strictly) $1_{m}$-preperiodic points of a polynomial map $\varphi_{d, c}$ defined by $\varphi_{d, c}(z) = z^d + c$ for all $c, z \in \mathcal{O}_{K}$ and the coefficient $c$, where $K$ is any number field of degree $n\geq 1$, $d>2$ is an integer and $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is any fixed (eventual period).
